output.reason: A 68-year-old with COPD reporting two days of worsening dyspnea now provoked by walking to the bathroom plus green phlegm needs hands-on assessment today with oxygen saturation, lung exam and chest imaging, which messaging cannot provide.
output.patientMessage: Please be seen in person today — urgent care or ED — for an oxygen-level check, lung exam and chest X-ray, since your breathlessness now happens just walking to the bathroom and your phlegm changed color. Call 911 right away if you struggle to speak in full sentences, feel confused or drowsy, your lips turn blue, or you have chest pain.
differential: Pneumonia or other complication (e.g. heart failure, PE) causing worsening dyspnea

redFlags.concern: Dyspnea at minimal exertion, worse than baseline
redFlags.quote: now I'm winded just walking to the bathroom

output.vitalSigns: No oxygen saturation, respiratory rate, heart rate or temperature reported; whether any measurement was taken is unknown.
output.evidenceLimitations: Severity cannot be graded remotely without oxygen saturation, work-of-breathing assessment or imaging.

citations.claim: Sustained worsening of dyspnea and sputum purulence beyond normal variation defines an acute COPD exacerbation requiring a change in therapy.
citations.limitation: Definition only; severity class not established without examination or oxygen measurement.

citations.claim: Pneumothorax, pulmonary embolism and heart failure also cause dyspnea in COPD patients, so chest imaging is advised rather than assuming COPD alone.
citations.limitation: Emergency-department reference; wheezing and exam findings are not reported for this patient.
